article_context: Body image in the first expert answer, following the ordered preparation steps for moisture-resistant tongue-and-groove gypsum boards and preceding the note that removing the surface layer does not reduce moisture resistance. It visually emphasizes controlled, technically correct preparation of the substrate for reliable tile adhesion.
image_reading: A worker’s hand holds a notched metal trowel against a wall covered with gray adhesive; straight vertical ridges and curved comb marks are already visible.
The trowel, hand, adhesive ridges, and a turquoise prepared area at the lower left dominate the close composition; the trowel and fresh adhesive are the naturally movable elements.

models.positive_prompt: The hand steadily draws the notched trowel upward through the fresh adhesive, extending clean parallel ridges at an even thickness. Fixed camera; by the final frame the newly combed strip is uniform and the trowel remains pressed to the wall.
models.scene_plan: Five-second fixed close-up. The hand immediately begins one steady upward trowel pass with moderate pressure, continuously combing the fresh adhesive. The pass develops through most of the shot, extending the existing ridge pattern without changing tools or direction. Near the end the motion eases, leaving a clearly uniform newly ridged strip while the trowel remains visible against the wall.

models.positive_prompt: With a smooth controlled upward pass, the hand combs the fresh adhesive into evenly spaced parallel ridges. Keep the camera fixed; end with a uniform ridged strip and the trowel still touching the wall.
models.scene_plan: A single five-second fixed shot focused on the working edge of the trowel. The hand makes one controlled upward pass at an even pace, with fresh adhesive flowing through the notches and settling into parallel ridges. The movement occupies nearly the full duration and slows naturally as the new strip becomes visibly even; the hand and tool stay recognizable in frame.

models.positive_prompt: Fixed close-up as the hand makes one concise upward trowel pass, combing the fresh adhesive into straight, even ridges. Finish with the new ridged section uniform and the trowel still visible against the wall.
models.scene_plan: Four-second fixed close-up with a shorter, focused upward pass. The trowel starts moving at once and travels a moderate distance, its notches forming straight ridges continuously. The hand decelerates only near the end, revealing an even combed section while the tool remains in contact and fully visible.

structured_intent.editorial_meaning: Correct, controlled substrate preparation and adhesive application create the reliable, even base needed for tile installation.
structured_intent.primary_action: The hand draws the notched trowel through fresh adhesive to form uniform parallel ridges.
structured_intent.semantic_invariant: The scene remains a precise, professional wall-preparation process for dependable tile adhesion.
structured_intent.terminal_state: A newly combed section of adhesive has even, continuous ridges, with the trowel still visible at the wall.
